recommendedTextbook.title: Junior English Project for Secondary Schools 1
recommendedTextbook.author: N. Grant, D. Olagoke, J. Southern

topics.topic: Parts of Speech: Nouns (Types, Functions and Pluralization Rules)
subtopics: Definition of nouns and identification in passages
Proper, common, collective, and abstract nouns
Countable vs uncountable nouns (much vs many, few vs little)
Rules of regular and irregular pluralization
objectives: Define nouns and categorize nouns into proper, common, abstract, and collective types
Apply correct plural forms for irregular nouns (child/children, tooth/teeth, ox/oxen)
Identify nouns in authentic Nigerian narrative texts

topics.topic: Pronouns: Personal, Possessive, Demonstrative & Relative Pronouns
subtopics: Definition of pronouns as noun substitutes to avoid monotony
Subjective vs objective personal pronouns (I/me, he/him, they/them)
Possessive pronouns vs possessive adjectives (mine vs my, theirs vs their)
Demonstrative pronouns (this, that, these, those)
objectives: Replace repetitive nouns with appropriate personal pronouns
Differentiate possessive pronouns from possessive determiners
Ensure antecedent-pronoun agreement in structured sentences

topics.topic: Verbs: Action Verbs, Auxiliary Verbs, Simple Present & Past Tenses
subtopics: Definition of verbs as action or state of being words
Primary auxiliary verbs (be, do, have) and modal auxiliaries
Simple present tense for habitual actions and general truths
Simple past tense and regular/irregular verb inflection
objectives: Distinguish main verbs from auxiliary verbs in sentences
Conjugate regular and irregular verbs into simple past tense forms
Formulate complete sentences describing daily routines in Nigeria

topics.topic: Speech Work: Monophthongs (Short and Long Vowel Contrasts)
subtopics: Vowel articulation: open, half-open, close positions
Contrasting short and long vowels: /i:/ vs /ɪ/ (seat vs sit), /u:/ vs /ʊ/ (fool vs full)
Contrasting /ɔ:/ vs /ɒ/ (cord vs cod, port vs pot) and transcription drills
objectives: Articulate English monophthongs with accurate tongue height and lip rounding
Pronounce minimal pairs accurately without Mother Tongue interference
Identify vowel sounds in examination word lists

topics.topic: Adjectives and Adverbs: Identification, Comparison and Modifying Roles
subtopics: Definition of adjectives as noun modifiers
Degrees of comparison of adjectives (positive, comparative, superlative)
Definition of adverbs and types (manner, time, place, degree)
Formation of adverbs from adjectives by adding -ly
objectives: Identify adjectives and adverbs in reading passages
Formulate regular and irregular comparisons (good/better/best, bad/worse/worst)
Use descriptive adverbs to enhance sentence vividness

topics.topic: Continuous Writing: Descriptive Composition ('My School / My Community')
subtopics: Features of descriptive writing (sensory details, spatial arrangement)
Paragraph development: topic sentence, supporting details, concluding sentence
Writing a 3-paragraph descriptive composition on 'My School'
objectives: Structure a coherent descriptive composition with introduction, body, and conclusion
Use vivid sensory adjectives to depict school buildings and compound life
Observe proper punctuation and paragraph indentation rules

topics.topic: Mid-Term Continuous Assessment & Speech Diagnostic Check
subtopics: Diagnostic evaluation on nouns, pronouns, verbs, speech sounds, and composition
Remedial grammar and phonetics clinic
objectives: Assess pupil grammatical fluency and phonetic accuracy

topics.topic: Prepositions and Conjunctions in Complex Sentence Construction
subtopics: Prepositions of place, time, and direction (in, on, at, into, under, across)
Prepositional phrases functioning as adjectival or adverbial modifiers
Coordinating conjunctions (FANBOYS: for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so)
Subordinating conjunctions (because, although, since, unless, while)
objectives: Use prepositions accurately without common local Nigerian errors (e.g., 'discuss about')
Join simple sentences into compound and complex sentences using conjunctions

topics.topic: Reading Comprehension: Skimming, Scanning and Context Clues
subtopics: Difference between skimming for main idea and scanning for specific facts
Deducing meanings of unfamiliar words using contextual clues
Answering direct and inferential comprehension questions on Nigerian folk stories
objectives: Scan a 300-word passage to retrieve specific dates, names, and facts within 2 minutes
Infer word meanings directly from surrounding sentence context

topics.topic: Literature in English: Introduction to Folktales, Myths and African Legends
subtopics: Definition of literature and three genres (prose, poetry, drama)
Features and moral themes of indigenous Nigerian folktales (Tortoise trickster tales)
Distinction between myths (explanations of creation) and legends (historical heroes like Moremi, Bayajidda)
objectives: Name the three primary genres of literature
Identify the moral lesson in a selected Nigerian tortoise fable
Differentiate folktales from historical legends

topics.topic: Figures of Speech: Simile and Metaphor in African Poetry
subtopics: Definition of figures of speech and figurative vs literal language
Simile: direct comparison using 'as' or 'like'
Metaphor: direct identification comparison without 'as' or 'like'
Identifying similes and metaphors in recommended African poems
objectives: Differentiate similes from metaphors with clear examples
Create 5 original similes rooted in Nigerian cultural realities

topics.topic: Comprehensive Termly Revision & Speech Sound Clinic
subtopics: Review of parts of speech, tenses, sentence joining, and composition
Speech sound pronunciation testing
objectives: Complete comprehensive JSS 1 English Studies revision

subtopics: Terminal examination on grammar, comprehension, composition, and literature
objectives: Complete JSS 1 English Studies Term 1 certification
